name: Mehuman
title: Eunuch at the court of King Ahasuerus
summary: Mehuman was one of the seven eunuchs (court officials) who served King Ahasuerus (Xerxes I) in the Persian Empire. He is mentioned in the book of Esther as one of those whom the king commanded to bring Queen Vashti during the great banquet. His role was limited, but he is part of the historical context for the story of Esther.

keyEvents.title: The King's Great Banquet
keyEvents.description: King Ahasuerus held a great feast in the citadel of Susa that lasted 180 days to display his wealth and splendor.

keyEvents.title: The King Orders the Eunuchs to Bring Vashti
keyEvents.description: On the seventh day, when the king was merry with wine, he commanded Mehuman and the other six eunuchs to bring Queen Vashti before him wearing the royal crown, so that her beauty might be displayed.

keyEvents.title: Queen Vashti's Refusal
keyEvents.description: Queen Vashti refused to come at the king's command delivered by the eunuchs, which made the king very angry.

keyEvents.title: The Consequences of Vashti's Refusal
keyEvents.description: Vashti's refusal led to counsel from the king's wise men and ultimately her removal as queen, paving the way for Esther's elevation.
